added_models.model: Decision-tree / exposure-safety model of NOVA patients (niraparib individualized starting dose)

dose.note: A decision-tree model of NOVA patients predicted that body weight <77 kg or platelets <150,000/uL should start niraparib at 200 mg without losing efficacy.
dose.quote: The analysis presented suggests that patients with baseline body weight of <77 kg or baseline platelets of <150 000/µl may benefit from a starting dose of 200 mg/day.
dose.judgement: A model fitted to NOVA patient data, not a preclinical system; in scope as an in-silico model used to choose dose. Its prediction (per-patient starting dose) was tested prospectively, so it is not a retrodiction.
dose.population: Platinum-sensitive recurrent ovarian cancer (NOVA safety population)

dose.note: NORA dosed 249 patients by the weight/platelet rule (235 at 200 mg); PFS benefit held regardless of BRCA status and toxicity was manageable.
dose.short: NORA: 200 mg ISD effective and safer
dose.quote: Individualized niraparib dosing is effective and safe and should be considered standard practice in this setting.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level. NORA has no fixed-dose comparator; PRIMA's stated fixed- vs individualized-dose comparison (Mirza 2023, doi 10.1002/cncr.34706) agrees.
dose.judgement: Paired by me (Berek 2018 model, NORA 2021 trial). Mirza 2023 states the comparison in PRIMA: 'similar dose intensity, similar efficacy, and improved safety were observed with the ISD compared with the FSD regimen'; it changes no status. The model stated 200 mg was effective and better tolerated, and patients dosed to it showed that, so margin_stated true. NCT03705156 has no posted results; FDA adopted the ISD in the 2020 label (PRIMA review not read).
dose.magnitude_basis: PFS benefit and haematologic toxicity at the 200 mg individualized starting dose vs the model's predicted benefit
dose.population: Platinum-sensitive recurrent ovarian cancer, China, BRCA-mutant and wild-type (NORA)

considered_not_added: Patient-derived ovarian cancer organoids (de Witte 2020 Cell Rep; Thorel 2025; Nanki 2020; Senkowski 2023; Ito 2023): organoid-patient comparisons are for carboplatin/paclitaxel only; PARP inhibitor (olaparib, niraparib) organoid responses were not compared with patients' PARPi outcomes.

Short-term HGSC organoids with RAD51 functional HR assay (Hill 2018 Cancer Discov): PARPi sensitivity correlated with organoid HR defect; olaparib, and the authors state patient-response prediction is untested.
RAD51 foci score in PDX / archival tumours (Castroviejo-Bermejo 2018 EMBO Mol Med; RECAP): breast cancer PDX and olaparib, not a member drug; no ovarian patient comparison for a member drug found.

BRCA-wild-type xenograft tumour-distribution model (Sun 2018 Oncotarget, niraparib): a retrodiction 'consistent with' NOVA non-gBRCA benefit, but the prediction concerns BRCA-wild-type tumours, outside the BRCA-mutant/HRD population, and the xenografts' HRD status is not given.
Ovarian PDX with niraparib in HR-deficient and proficient tumours (AlHilli 2016 Gynecol Oncol): model data only, no patient comparison found.
Tumour genomic LOH / HRD classifiers (ARIEL2 for rucaparib, Myriad myChoice in PRIMA): patient-selection biomarkers measured in the patients' own tumours, not model systems.

FDA 2017 niraparib exposure-safety logistic regression (208447 review): part of the same patient-data dose model; FDA did not use exposure-efficacy for dose selection, so folded into niraparib-isd-model rather than tracked separately.
Niraparib PBPK / population PK models (hepatic impairment 2026, PRIMA popPK 2024): no prospective patient comparison of a model-chosen dose found within budget.

Pamiparib, senaparib, 2X-121 (stenoparib) DRP, veliparib: no model-vs-patient comparison found beyond the draft's tracks; stenoparib's DRP ex-vivo/transcriptomic predictor is in a non-BRCA-selected population with press-release-only results.
